knownLimitations: Real Chrome window lost OS-level foreground focus late in the initial test pass (document.visibilityState stuck 'hidden' despite repeated real interaction and waits up to 20s+, including in a freshly created tab in the same window); cumulativeFrameCount honestly stayed frozen at 0 rather than being fabricated.

claude-in-chrome's resize_window changes OS window bounds but not window.innerWidth/innerHeight (fixed virtual framebuffer), blocking real interactive mobile-viewport R3F verification in that surface.

Sandboxed Claude_Browser pane achieved a genuine 390x844 viewport but click interaction and screenshot capture became unreliable near the end of the mobile test attempt, consistent with SYS-70's documented finding that this pane never reliably renders/interacts with R3F content.

During the pre-merge audit replay, document.visibilityState was stuck 'hidden' again; the native 'timeupdate' event did not fire automatically despite audio.currentTime genuinely changing. A manual dispatchEvent(new Event('timeupdate')) was used to verify the fixed fallback component without modifying its code — once delivered, the component behaved exactly as expected (see noWebglEvidence.staticPosesConfirmed).

None of these limitations affected the dramaturgy/narrative evidence itself (timeline, idle, cues, signature, pause/seek/loop, zone/track reset, no-WebGL composition), all obtained successfully either directly or via the manually-dispatched timeupdate event.
